title: The Agent Builder test asserts the UI against the very constants it is meant to guard, so it can never fail on catalog drift
repro: design — src/modules/agent-builder/agent-builder.test.tsx:137 loops `for (const tool of KNOWN_TOOL_IDS)` asserting a button exists for each, and :143 asserts the provider <select> options `toEqual([...KNOWN_PROVIDER_IDS])`. Both constants are the hardcoded arrays in form.tsx. Deleting 30 ids from form.tsx (or adding openrouter to the sidecar) leaves the suite green.
notes: Special-general mixture / special-casing to satisfy a test: the assertion is a tautology (UI rendered from X equals X), so it certifies the drift in findings 1-3 rather than catching it. Consequence: the one automated guard over this seam is inert, and a reviewer reading the test believes the list is covered. Smallest fix: assert against a checked-in fixture of the sidecar's agent_selectable_tool_ids()/provider_ids() output (or fetch it in a contract test), not against the frontend constant.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: the panel test iterates the imported KNOWN_TOOL_IDS and asserts the provider options equal the imported KNOWN_PROVIDER_IDS, the same constants the UI renders from, so it cannot detect drift from the sidecar catalog/registry; nothing else in src/ or scripts/ references the frontend list.

title: The context badge's visibility is gated on string equality with a user-facing sentence minted 850 lines away
repro: design — ChatSidebar.tsx:1191 renders the badge only when `contextBadge !== "Context: none"`; that exact literal is produced by describeContext at :2044. Change the copy at :2044 to "No panel context" and the badge renders on every boot with the standing dead row the R9 stray-item audit removed; change it at :1191 only and the badge disappears entirely. Neither edit fails a test.
notes: Obviousness (APOSD #16) + duplicated truth: a render decision is encoded in prose. The function already knows whether there is context; it flattens that to a string and the caller re-derives it by comparison. Consequence: a copy edit silently changes behaviour, in either direction, with no failing test. Smallest fix: return a discriminated value ({kind:'none'} | {kind:'panels', text}) and branch on kind.

refuter.reason: The coupling is exactly as described: the badge is hidden by comparing against the literal 'Context: none' that describeContext returns 850 lines away. But nothing is broken today; it is a latent maintainability hazard that fires only if someone edits one of the two strings, so low rather than medium.

title: "The focused symbol" is extracted three different ways with three different rules, coupled only by a comment
repro: design — the same panel-context bus is read by (a) ChatSidebar.describeContext:2053-2061 (symbol -> ticker, raw case, also reads timeframe), (b) SuggestionChips.useFocusedSymbol:50-66 (symbol -> ticker, uppercased), (c) context-provider.captureTerminalState:276-278 (focused chart's symbol, else charts[0], else watchlist.selected, else watchlist[0]). Focus an equity panel publishing {ticker:'infy'}: the badge says 'Context: … (infy)', the chips offer 'Research $INFY', and the agent's terminal snapshot reports focusedSymbol null (it only looks at chart* sources).
notes: Repetition of nontrivial logic (APOSD #4/#15); the coupling is asserted by a comment at SuggestionChips.tsx:45-46 ('mirroring describeContext in ChatSidebar') rather than by structure, and the three have ALREADY diverged on casing and on which sources count. Consequence: the badge, the suggestion chips and what the agent is actually told about 'what you're looking at' can disagree in the same instant -- directly against the product's context-fidelity promise. Smallest fix: one exported focusedSymbolFromBus(bus) in context-provider.ts, consumed by all three.

refuter.reason: The duplication and rule divergence are real, but the concrete repro is wrong and the actual defect is different. PanelHost sets focusedSource to the dockview panel id ('equity-overview', 'chart'), while the panels publish under different bus keys ('equity', and `chart-${api.id}` = 'chart-chart'). So describeContext and SuggestionChips.useFocusedSymbol never find the focused panel's event: the badge reads 'Context: equity-overview' with no ticker and symbol chips never render. captureTerminalState then reports charts[0]'s or the watchlist's symbol (not null) as focusedSymbol. Consequence: focusing an Equity Overview for INFY while the chart shows SPY tells the agent the focused symbol is SPY, which breaks deixis. Fix shape: one focusedSymbolFromBus plus a single source-key convention (publish under the dockview panel id).

title: The command palette's agent row re-parses an id prefix instead of reading the agent object it already holds
repro: design — CommandPalette.tsx:184 does `setActiveAgent(item.id.replace(/^agent:/, ''))` while the same PaletteItem carries `agentSummary` (set at store/command-palette.ts:220-226) whose `.id` is the unprefixed value. If the corpus id scheme changes (e.g. to 'agents/<id>'), the strip silently no-ops and the palette sets the active agent to the literal 'agents/buffett', which resolves to no agent -- the persona chip falls back to humanizeAgentId and sends route to a nonexistent agent.
notes: Information leakage (APOSD #4): the id encoding chosen in the store is decoded by string surgery in a component, so the encoding is known in two places. The failure is silent rather than loud because ChatSidebar.activeAgent resolves an unknown id to null and humanizeAgentId happily renders it. Smallest fix: `setActiveAgent(item.agentSummary.id)` -- the data is already on the item.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: the agent row decodes item.id with replace(/^agent:/,'') even though the item already carries agentSummary with the unprefixed id. It works today, custom 'agent:custom:x' included, so this is latent encoding leakage only, correctly rated low.

title: Every mouse move and pan re-renders the entire 1,585-line ChartPanel: it subscribes to the sync bus's crosshair/visibleRange objects unconditionally and broadcasts on every move, with no peer chart to receive them
repro: Move the mouse across the chart -> onCrosshair (ChartPanel.tsx:852-855) -> setCrosshair creates a new {time, source, seq} object per event (chart-sync.ts:73-76) -> ChartPanel's own selector `useChartSyncBus(s => s.crosshair)` (:323) changes identity -> full component re-render (toolbar ladder, chips, inspector) at pointer-event rate, even though syncSubscriptions.crosshair is false and the chart is a singleton (index.ts:30). Same for every visible-range change while panning (:857-866 -> :324).
notes: Performance as design (APOSD #18) + pass-through state: broadcast payloads are selected as React state instead of being read in a store subscription callback. Consequence: jank on the most interactive surface, worse with drawings/indicators. Fix: move the three subscriber effects to useChartSyncBus.subscribe (no re-render), and only broadcast when some other panel is subscribed - or delete the bus (see COD-4).

refuter.reason: Mechanism holds: ChartPanel selects s.crosshair and s.visibleRange as React state and broadcasts a new object on every crosshair move/range change, so the whole panel re-renders at pointer rate even with sync off and no peer. But the only cascading effect (panel-context publish) depends on primitives and does not re-fire, and no jank was measured; the cost is a wasted re-render, and the fix is subsumed by deleting the dead bus (COD-4). Downgraded to low.

title: Panel minimum-size policy is locked inside the React host: only the boot restore grows sub-minimum panels, layout templates re-derive the same numbers as magic widths, and the table has drifted from the registered components
repro: Save a named layout with a squeezed panel (a blob saved before min-sizes, or one captured mid-squeeze), then Load it from Settings or the Load dialog. loadWorkspace -> deserializeWorkspace -> api.fromJSON (workspace.ts:265, 432) restores the sub-minimum size. The grow sweep enforceConstraintsAfterRestore runs only in PanelHost's boot finally (PanelHost.tsx:166-186), so the panel stays squeezed until relaunch. Separately: PANEL_MIN_SIZE has 'chat-sidebar' (PanelHost.tsx:67), which is no longer a registered component (chat/index.ts:11 says stale chat-sidebar panels are remapped); 'broker-order-entry' (:69) belongs to the removed trading path; and the research surfaces 'brief-panel' and 'notes-panel' have no entry, so they get the 300x180 default.
notes: Information hiding placed at the wrong layer. The policy ('no panel below N px') is domain knowledge about PanelSpec components, yet it is a private const inside a component file. So (a) workspace.ts, the code that actually calls fromJSON, cannot apply it; (b) layout-templates.ts restates it as prose and hand-derived thresholds (RESEARCH_COCKPIT_MIN_WIDTH 1180, 'keeps >=30% so its 360px panel minimum holds') that will drift the next time a minimum changes; (c) nothing checks the keys against collectPanels(), hence the dead and missing entries. This is temporal decomposition: 'grow after restore' is tied to 'boot' rather than to 'fromJSON'. Smallest fix: move PANEL_MIN_SIZE and both helpers to src/lib/panel-sizing.ts; call the grow sweep from deserializeWorkspace (deferred with setTimeout, as the boot path does); have layout-templates compute fit widths from the table; add a parity test (every key is a registered component, every registered component is keyed or deliberately defaulted).

refuter.reason: The structure claims are accurate. PANEL_MIN_SIZE is private to PanelHost. The grow sweep runs only in the boot finally. Named-layout load (loadWorkspace -> deserializeWorkspace -> fromJSON) never grows sub-minimum panels. 'chat-sidebar' and 'broker-order-entry' are dead keys; broker-order-entry goes with trading. 'brief-panel' and 'notes-panel' fall to the 300x180 default. The functional repro, though, needs a legacy or sub-minimum blob: onDidAddPanel applies constraints to every loaded panel, so new saves cannot capture a sub-minimum sash. No clipped brief or notes state was shown. This is a maintainability risk plus an edge case, so medium becomes low.

title: Three stores own 'which transcript is live' and none knows a stream is in flight: switching a chat tab mid-stream drops the reply, archives a forever-pending partial and unlocks a concurrent send; entering a research space discards the active tab's transcript
repro: (a) Chat tab 1: send a prompt, and while the answer streams click '+' or another tab in the space strip (ChatSidebar.tsx:1146 / 1167, not disabled while streaming) -> chat-history.loadMessages/clear sets streamingMessageId=null, the run keeps calling appendAssistantDelta(id) on an id no longer in `messages` (silently a no-op), finalize is a no-op too; switching back restores the archived snapshot {content:'Partial ', pending:true} forever. `streaming` flips false, so the composer and the queue drain (ChatSidebar.tsx:1105-1111) start a SECOND stream while run 1 is still live. Proven: code/evidence/frontend-stores-proof.test.ts.txt P2. (b) Chat tab 2 has a conversation; create or load a research space from a plain workspace -> research-spaces.switchSpace(null, next) -> restoreSpace -> chat.loadMessages/clear (research-spaces.ts:178-186) without saving the live transcript anywhere; agent-spaces still thinks tab 2 is live, so tab 2's conversation is gone and the next tab switch archives the RESEARCH transcript under tab 2's id.
evidence: src/store/agent-spaces.ts:43-64, src/store/research-spaces.ts:178-198, src/store/chat-history.ts:236-237, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:382, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:886-935, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1105-1111, src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:1146, src/lib/workspace.ts:363-369, src/lib/workspace.ts:627, docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/code/evidence/frontend-stores-proof-output.txt
notes: Information hiding / better-together violated: the live transcript is a shared mutable buffer that two independent 'space' stores overwrite through chat-history's public loadMessages/clear, and loadMessages unconditionally nulls streamingMessageId. Consequences: a (possibly paid Tier-B / deep) research answer is silently lost, the thread shows a stuck pending bubble, two agent runs can race (and a late brief publish from run 1 then passes brief.ts:198-205 because the stale_run guard only applies in the in_flight phase), and a chat tab's conversation is destroyed on entering a research space. Smallest fix: make chat-history the single thread owner (threads: Record<threadId, ChatMessage[]>, activeThreadId), address every streaming write by (threadId, messageId) so a background thread keeps receiving deltas, and make agent tabs and research spaces two naming/persistence policies over it. Interim guard: disable the space strip (and block research-space switches) while streamingMessageId !== null, or abortRef.current?.abort() before the switch.

refuter.reason: Holds as stated. agent-spaces.switchTo/newSpace archive the live messages and call chat-history.loadMessages/clear, both of which unconditionally set streamingMessageId=null; the space-strip buttons carry no streaming guard; appendAssistantDelta maps over messages so deltas for the archived id are silent no-ops; with streaming=false the composer sends directly instead of queueing and the queue drain restarts, so a second run can start while run 1 is live. Part (b) also holds: research-spaces.switchSpace(null, next) restores/clears the live transcript without saving it, while agent-spaces.activeId still points at the old tab.

title: The workflow store is a complete but dead SSE consumer; the node editor streams runs privately, so the 'Show a native desktop notification' node never notifies while reporting notified:true
repro: Node editor: build data.fetch_quote -> action.notify_desktop, click Run -> NodeEditorPanel.tsx:386 POSTs /workflow/run and parses the SSE into LOCAL state (setRunState, :399-431); nothing calls useWorkflowStore.appendEvent (grep: zero production callers of appendEvent/runWorkflow/selectRunLog/selectActiveRunLog outside the store), so pendingNotifications (only filled by appendEvent, workflow.ts:203-220) stays empty and useDesktopNotificationBridge (desktop-notification.ts:92-110, mounted page.tsx:43) never fires. The node's output row shows notified:true (sidecar builtin.py:337-344).
notes: Strategic-over-tactical / duplicated truth: two SSE parsers for one wire (workflow.ts:114-167 + :317-337 vs the node editor's own), and the feature that depends on the store (desktop notifications) is fed by the parser nobody runs. The header comment and the sidecar docstring describe a dispatcher pipeline that does not exist, and the node reports success. The dead runWorkflow also has latent defects if it is revived as-is: a mid-stream failure after run-start is swallowed (workflow.ts:299-302) with no synthetic run-error, so activeRun never clears; there is no AbortController/cancel, and `runs` is unbounded. Smallest fix: in NodeEditorPanel's event loop call useWorkflowStore.getState().appendEvent(event) (one line), or better, drive the panel from runWorkflow + selectRunLog and delete the private parser; add a terminal run-error on stream failure and an abort signal.

refuter.reason: Holds. grep finds no production caller of useWorkflowStore.appendEvent/runWorkflow/selectRunLog (only the store itself at workflow.ts:270); NodeEditorPanel POSTs /workflow/run and parses SSE into local state only; action.notify_desktop is a server-side node (partitioned to the sidecar) whose handler only logs and returns notified:true, so the mounted notification bridge never sees an intent. With no separate alert store in src/store, this node is the product's only desktop-alert path, so high stands.

title: drainNotifications() clears ALL pending intents, including ones captured while the bridge was awaiting the send, so a second notification that arrives mid-flush is silently dropped
repro: Bridge flush: snapshot=[A]; await _sendOne(A); meanwhile appendEvent adds B; bridge calls drainNotifications() which empties [A,B]; the rerun loop finds nothing -> B is never shown. Proven: code/evidence/frontend-stores-proof.test.ts.txt P3 (sent ['a'], 0 left pending).
notes: Interface shape makes correct use impossible: 'drain everything' cannot be combined with an async send of a snapshot. Latent today (finding COD-frontend-stores-2 means nothing feeds the queue) but it bites the moment that is fixed, and a workflow firing several alerts in quick succession is the normal case. Smallest fix: replace drainNotifications with takeNotifications() that atomically returns and clears the current queue BEFORE sending, or drain(ids) that removes only the sent intents.

refuter.reason: Holds and is latent as stated. The bridge snapshots intents, awaits _sendOne for each, then calls drainNotifications(), which empties the whole slice including an intent appended mid-await; the subscriber's re-flush only sets rerun=true, and the rerun iteration then reads an empty slice.

title: The keybindings store persists and advertises 11 remappable shortcuts but owns no dispatch: only agent.toggle honours a remap, six defaults (mod+s, mod+o, mod+, and mod+1..4) have no handler at all, and four are hard-coded elsewhere
repro: Settings -> Keybindings ('Remap any shortcut', SettingsPanel.tsx:1413) lists DEFAULT_KEYBINDINGS; remap 'Accept all proposed changes' to mod+shift+a -> ⌘↵ still accepts (hard-coded ChatSidebar.tsx:554-561) and ⌘⇧A does nothing. Press ⌘S / ⌘O / ⌘, / ⌘1 (the shown defaults) -> nothing happens: grep finds no keydown handler for them. Only AgentDock.tsx:70 reads bindingFor(). Mode ⌥1/⌥2 is matched on event.code in ChatSidebar.tsx:541-547; the palette's ⌘K is hard-coded in CommandPalette.tsx:77.

Only AgentDock reads bindingFor(); the palette hard-codes mod+k, ChatSidebar hard-codes alt+Digit and mod+Enter/Backspace; no keydown handler anywhere in src handles mod+s, mod+o, mod+, or mod+1..4, and the Tauri menu is Menu::default (no such accelerators). matchesEvent only enforces Shift when requested, so mod+b also fires on mod+shift+b.

title: No fetch slice carries a request generation: a slower stale response overwrites the newer one; SEC loadFilings even rewrites activeIdentifier back to the stale symbol, and earnings shows one window while the picker says another
repro: SEC panel: the default AAPL load is in flight (cold sidecar / slow EDGAR); the user submits MSFT -> MSFT resolves, then AAPL resolves -> set({activeIdentifier: 'AAPL', filingsStatus: 'ready'}) and the panel reverts to AAPL while the input shows MSFT (proven: code/evidence/frontend-stores-proof.test.ts.txt P1). An AAPL error arriving late likewise overwrites MSFT's ready status with an error banner, because filingsStatus/filingsError are single scalars for all keys. Earnings: the default 7-day load is in flight; the user applies 30 days (EarningsCalendarPanel.tsx:152) -> lastDays=30 immediately, the 30-day payload lands, then the 7-day payload lands and replaces `upcoming` -> the table shows a 7-day window under a 30-day picker.
notes: Pull-complexity-down violated: the panels add userInteractedRef to stop RE-FIRES, but the in-flight request is not cancelled and the store commits any late response. Root: every async slice (sec, earnings, analyst-ratings, quant, macro) hand-rolls status/error/cache with no shared primitive, so staleness is decided nowhere. The panel's own header then labels the stale data correctly, so this is a medium 'wrong thing shown for the request' rather than mislabeled money data. Smallest fix: a per-slice generation counter (const gen = ++get().filingsGen; ... if (gen !== get().filingsGen) return;) or an AbortController per slice; stop loadFilings from writing activeIdentifier (the panel already sets it at submit); key status/error by cache key.

refuter.reason: Holds. sec.loadFilings commits any late response and writes activeIdentifier back to its own identifier, with single scalar filingsStatus/filingsError; the panel's userInteractedRef only stops re-fires, not the in-flight default AAPL request. earnings.loadUpcoming sets lastDays eagerly and commits whichever payload lands last. The race needs a slow default load (cold sidecar / EDGAR), which is the normal first-mount situation.

title: agents.refreshCustom turns an HTTP failure into a successful empty list, so a sidecar error reads as 'you have no custom agents' and the builder's error+Retry branch is unreachable
repro: Make GET /custom-agents return 500 (e.g. corrupt store) -> agents.ts:223-227 sets {customAgents: [], customSummaries: [], customStatus: 'ready', customError: null} -> AgentBuilderPanel renders the empty state (:457) instead of the error branch (:443-455), and the chat picker drops every custom persona. After a successful save the panel awaits refreshCustom() (AgentBuilderPanel.tsx:206); a failing list call then makes the user's agents appear deleted.
notes: Define-errors-out-of-existence misapplied: it converts a failure into a false fact. The sibling slice (refreshFirstParty, same file) uses sidecarGet and surfaces the error; this one hand-rolls fetch and soft-fails, and only a thrown network error reaches the error state. An active custom persona whose summary vanished also degrades the chat header silently. Smallest fix: use sidecarGet<CustomAgentWire[]>('/custom-agents') and let the catch set customStatus:'error' with the SidecarError detail (a 3-line change, the same shape as refreshFirstParty).

refuter.reason: The soft-fail branch is real (non-2xx -> ready + empty list), but the stated repro is wrong: an unhandled 500 (e.g. a corrupt store raising in agents_store.list_agents) leaves the sidecar via ServerErrorMiddleware with no CORS headers, so the cross-origin webview fetch rejects with a TypeError and the catch DOES set customStatus:'error' and show Retry. The soft-fail only triggers on CORS-headered non-2xx (a 404 on a stale sidecar, an HTTPException), which the list route never raises. So it is a latent inconsistency with refreshFirstParty, not a live 'agents appear deleted' path; downgraded to low.

title: Durable research-space turns drop message status: a failed, stopped or still-streaming partial answer is archived and later restored as a clean, finished assistant reply; agent-space tabs are not persisted at all
repro: In a research space, let a research stream fail mid-answer (the message has error set and partial content) -> leave and re-enter the space (or relaunch) -> captureLiveTranscript (research-spaces.ts:48-57) kept it (the only filter is non-empty content) and turnsToMessages (:60-67) rebuilds it with no error/stopped/pending flag -> the truncated text renders as a normal answer and rides into the next request's `history` (ChatSidebar.tsx:749-753).
